memo.verdict: Neutral; park; conviction medium. MTU Aero Engines (MTX-DE) at €368.1 on 2026-09-24 is a cause-for-concern-clearing case in a high-quality aftermarket annuity business, not an earnings-growth case; the clearing is real and evidenced, but what it buys is cash conversion and a dividend, not earnings growth inside the 12 to 20 percent band, so the modal return is a C (14.3 percent a year at eighteen months, 11.5 percent a year at three years) against a 20 percent bar, with a 12 to 26 percent mark-to-market downside beneath it. The park rule is not triggered (management C, business quality B, predictability B, trackability A); the park is on the return. Two triggers progress the case to Early-Stage: the price at or below about €342 with the operating indicators intact (the level at which the modal path clears 20 percent a year over eighteen months), or the Q4 2026 results in February 2027 guiding FY2027 cash conversion at or above 60 percent with the MRO margin above 8.0 percent, which would move the multiple to the 17.7x to 18.0x anchors (17 to 19 percent a year) and, with the 40 percent payout restored, argue a B. Invalidation: grounded GTF aircraft not below 200 units by Q1 2027; FY2027 cash conversion guided below 60 percent in February 2027; the MRO margin not stabilised above 8.0 percent by Q1 2027.
case: - The change is external, transient by its own arithmetic, and clearing. A partner's manufacturing defect (the Pratt & Whitney GTF powder-metal recall of July 2023) turned an aftermarket annuity into a cash problem: compensation of $1.0bn in 2024 and $360m in 2025, cash conversion of 24 percent and 39 percent of adjusted net income in those years, a share price that fell to €265 within the last year, while adjusted EPS compounded from €10.96 in FY2023 to €17.79 in FY2025. Compensation is $250m in 2026 and then ends; groundings are -25 percent year-to-date; conversion was 59 percent in H1 2026 and the FY2026 floor was raised to 50 percent on 30 July 2026, with a 2030 target of 75 to 99 percent.

- The demand behind the annuity is undisputed: commercial MRO +29 percent organic in US dollars in H1 2026 against a low-to-mid teens guide; flight hours 106 percent of 2019; GTF flight hours +22 percent; ten-year narrowbody airframe backlogs; retirements at 0.4 percent a quarter; engine MRO projected from US$70bn to over US$100bn by 2036; a €30.4bn backlog. External forces B; the headwinds (castings and forgings on 12 to 18-month lead times; the dollar beyond the 2026 hedge; fuel at $152 and Middle East traffic -8 percent in August 2026; CFM taking A320neo share with 86 percent of Farnborough 2026 narrowbody orders) are moderate and contained.

- The internal change is a new team executing the old plan, and it is real: the screen's rule is met (chief executive change plus a guidance increase); the false-positive checks pass (a five-year contract; the raise followed a delivered half). The 2030 targets were set under the predecessor and none has been raised. Internal forces B.
counter_case: - The "false friend", at full force: MTU's record margins are a temporary artefact of the crisis they appear to have survived. OEM margins above 30 percent for three quarters rest on a spare-engine delivery ratio of about 23 percent against a normal 15 percent, forced by grounded fleets, and on V2500 spares from a fleet whose retirements accelerate at $152 fuel; management itself projects declining spare ratios, and Deutsche Bank expects H2 2026 Airbus deliveries to shift the mix toward installed engines. Meanwhile the growth is in an 8 percent margin MRO business that pre-finances its own shop visits, so receivables (€4,600m at June 2026, +€385m in H1 2026) absorb the cash the compensation no longer takes, and conversion stays near 50 to 60 percent through 2028 rather than rising to 75 percent; Fitch models working-capital outflows of 3 percent of revenue through 2029, and expert calls put GTF supply normalisation at 2027 or 2028 with shop visits averaging 120 to 130 days. Redburn (Sell, €355) and UBS (Sell, €320) hold this view; Bernstein's own FY2026 free-cash-flow estimate of €429m sits below the guidance floor; the risks research's competing-hypotheses matrix picks this profile as its winner with one hard inconsistency against ten for the bull profile. On that reading earnings stall near €19 to €20, the multiple stays at 15x, and the shares are worth about €300 to €330.

- The record concedes: the OEM margin is at a mix peak and will fall as Airbus deliveries rise in H2 2026; the receivables lag the operational clearing by a year or more; the record's own earnings growth is below the band; part of the discount is structural and is carried only as a 0.7x haircut; the plausibly worse drop-through takes the return to F (7.3 percent a year at 17.0x; under 1 percent at 15.4x). And no division covers the enterprise value: at the propulsion peers' about 20x EV/EBIT, FY2025 OEM segment EBIT of €872m (30.4 percent of €2,870m) is worth €17.4bn, 87 percent of the €19,968m enterprise value; at the lowest named multiple of 13x it is €11.3bn, 57 percent; both divisions at 13x (€1,351m x 13 = €17.6bn) fall 12 percent short. There is no bounded-downside argument; the downside is the multiple, and it is not bounded: -12 percent to 14.70x, -26 percent to 12.26x, -32 percent to €251 on the risks research's 14x EV/EBIT.
triggers: - Progress triggers: the price at or below about €342 with the operating indicators intact; or the Q4 2026 results (February 2027) guiding FY2027 cash conversion at or above 60 percent with the MRO margin above 8.0 percent, which moves the multiple to 17.7x to 18.0x (17 to 19 percent a year) and, with the 40 percent payout restored, argues a B.

- The four things the case turns on, with the record's odds: (a) FY2027 conversion guided at or above 60 percent in February 2027, probable, about 65 percent; (b) the OEM segment margin above 28 percent through FY2028, plausible, about 55 percent; (c) the MRO margin recovering from 7.9 percent toward 8.5 percent by 2028, plausible, about 55 percent; (d) the multiple returning to the median less a mix discount (17.0x) once (a) is proven, probable conditional on (a), about 90 percent; the cleared-and-re-rated branch about 0.65 x 0.90 = 0.58, "probable, a little better than even".

- Invalidate levels: grounded GTF aircraft not below 200 units by Q1 2027; FY2027 conversion guidance at the Q4 2026 results not above 60 percent; the MRO margin not stabilised above 8.0 percent by Q1 2027; a V2500 retirement rate above 2 percent a year; a new airworthiness directive on the GTF Advantage; FY2027 consensus EPS cut below €19.5; receivables still rising at end-2027.

- Alarm levels: quarterly aircraft on ground plateauing in H2 2026; FY2026 conversion outturn below 55 percent; the OEM margin below 28 percent for two quarters; the MRO margin below 7.5 percent; another +€300m of receivables in a half; a new RTX programme charge; any Advantage-specific inspection directive; FY2026 EPS below €18.0; FY2026 free cash flow below €500m; the FY2026 dividend below €4.00; military growth below 10 percent; EUR/USD above 1.25; the 24-month-forward P/E below 14.7x with the operating indicators intact.

- Watch dates: Q3 2026 results 29 October 2026; the GTF Advantage entry into service H2 2026; the EUMET engine-study funding decision after end-September 2026; inspections and compensation wrapping up by year-end 2026; the Q4 2026 results February 2027; the May 2027 AGM (FY2026 dividend, payout policy); the Airbus-Pratt dispute settlement; RTX's quarterly GTF disclosures; Airbus's monthly deliveries.

- Open checks not possible from the inputs: overlap with the framework's own track-record and lessons files and with the Wisdom Library's negative archetypes (the nearest named archetype is the risks research's "false friend"); the thematics were read from the research because no live thematics file was among the inputs; the raise-to-lower revision ratio could not be verified because raise and lower counts were not shown.
